mcat_description.short: FRP Modular Toilet is a prefabricated, self-contained sanitation cabin made from Fibre Reinforced Plastic (FRP/fibreglass), sold as a ready-to-install unit for construction sites, public spaces, and rural sanitation programs.
mcat_description.long: FRP Modular Toilets are factory-built, single-piece or panel-assembled sanitation structures constructed from fibreglass reinforced plastic, offering high corrosion resistance, weather durability, and low maintenance in outdoor and semi-permanent deployments. Units are available in Indian-style (squat pan) and Western-style (ceramic commode) configurations, with optional integrated water tanks, wash basins, ventilation, and bio-digester waste systems. They are widely deployed under government sanitation schemes such as Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, at construction sites, public events, and rural/semi-urban locations lacking permanent sewage infrastructure. The modular design enables quick assembly, disassembly, and relocation, making them suitable for both temporary and long-term fixed installations.

market_context: FRP Modular Toilets in India are a well-established product category driven primarily by construction sector demand and government sanitation programs including Swachh Bharat Abhiyan. The dominant commercial form is the single-unit prefabricated FRP cabin available in Indian-style (squat) and Western-style (commode) configurations, with combined toilet+bathroom units being a significant and growing sub-segment as confirmed by both buyer call data and manufacturer product ranges. Key manufacturing hubs include Pune/Pimpri-Chinchwad (Maharashtra), Ahmedabad (Gujarat), New Delhi/NCR, Hyderabad (Telangana), and Jamshedpur (Jharkhand), with pan-India distribution networks. Wall thickness is a primary quality differentiator — market evidence shows a range from 2mm (economy) to 8–30mm (premium/sandwich panel) across manufacturers. Standard cabin dimensions cluster around 3×3 ft to 4×4 ft footprint with 7–8 ft height; combined toilet+bathroom units extend to 4×6 ft or 6×4 ft. Waste management options include simple septic tank connection, integrated bio-digester (anaerobic bacteria-based, no external sewage required), and chemical toilet systems. No single BIS IS standard was found specifically mandating FRP portable toilet construction (single source — low confidence); quality claims are manufacturer-self-certified against general FRP material standards. The term 'fiber toilet' or 'fiber bathroom' is the dominant colloquial buyer vocabulary in the Indian market, used interchangeably with 'FRP modular toilet.' Sintex is a recognised trade name in this space, though the broader market is highly fragmented with hundreds of regional manufacturers.
